topic: asking a friend to pet-sit
title: ¿Puedes cuidar a Misi?
titleEn: Can You Take Care of Misi?
text:
Laura: Hola, Mateo. Te escribo para pedirte un favor. El viernes me voy para Cartagena y vuelvo el martes. ¿Puedes cuidar a Misi?
Mateo: ¡Claro! ¿Qué tengo que hacer?
Laura: Dale comida por la mañana y por la noche. La comida está al lado de la nevera. También tienes que cambiarle el agua. Y las matas del balcón necesitan agua el domingo.
Mateo: Listo. ¿Y las llaves?
Laura: Se las dejo al portero el jueves. ¡Mil gracias! Te traigo dulces de Cartagena.
translation:
Laura: Hi, Mateo. I'm writing to ask you a favor. On Friday I'm going to Cartagena, and I'm coming back on Tuesday. Can you take care of Misi?
Mateo: Of course! What do I have to do?
Laura: Feed her in the morning and at night. The food is next to the fridge. You also have to change her water. And the plants on the balcony need water on Sunday.
Mateo: OK. And the keys?
Laura: I'll leave them with the doorman on Thursday. Thanks a million! I'll bring you some sweets from Cartagena.

questions.q: Why does Laura write to Mateo?
options: To invite him on a trip to Cartagena
To ask him to take care of her pet
To ask him to help her move this week
To lend him her car while she is away
questions.explain: Laura asks '¿Puedes cuidar a Misi?' and then explains how to feed her.

questions.q: When is Laura coming back?
questions.explain: Laura writes 'El viernes me voy para Cartagena y vuelvo el martes'.

questions.q: Laura writes about 'las matas del balcón'. What are 'matas'?
questions.explain: They are on the balcony and 'necesitan agua el domingo', so 'matas' are plants.

topic: language exchange meetings at a café
title: Intercambio de idiomas
text:
¿QUIERES PRACTICAR INGLÉS O ESPAÑOL?

Somos un grupo de colombianos y extranjeros. Nos reunimos todos los jueves, de 6:30 a 8:30 p. m., en un café de La Candelaria (Calle 12 # 3-45).

Primero hablamos una hora en español y después una hora en inglés. Hay mesas para todos los niveles. No es una clase y no hay profesores. Es gratis: solo pagas tu bebida.
Si quieres venir, escríbenos al 310 555 4192. ¡Te esperamos!
translation:
DO YOU WANT TO PRACTICE ENGLISH OR SPANISH?

We are a group of Colombians and foreigners. We meet every Thursday, from 6:30 to 8:30 p.m., at a café in La Candelaria (Calle 12 # 3-45).

First we speak Spanish for an hour and then English for an hour. There are tables for all levels. It isn't a class and there are no teachers. It's free: you only pay for your drink.
If you want to come, write to us at 310 555 4192. We hope to see you there!

questions.q: What is this ad for?
options: An English course for young children
A new café in La Candelaria
Jobs for English and Spanish teachers
questions.explain: The group meets every Thursday and speaks 'una hora en español y después una hora en inglés'.

questions.q: What do you have to pay for?
questions.explain: The ad says 'Es gratis: solo pagas tu bebida'.

questions.q: 'Somos un grupo de colombianos y extranjeros.' Who are the 'extranjeros'?
questions.explain: The word is paired with 'colombianos', so it means people who are not Colombian.

topic: coworkers talking about their weekend
title: ¿Cómo te fue el fin de semana?
text:
—Buenos días, Paola. ¿Cómo te fue el fin de semana?
—Muy bien, Andrés. El sábado almorcé con mis papás y por la noche salí a bailar con unas amigas. ¿Y a ti?
—Bien, pero no descansé. Mi esposa y yo pintamos todo el apartamento. Terminamos el domingo a las diez de la noche.
—¡Uy, qué juicioso! Yo, en cambio, no hice nada útil: el domingo dormí hasta las once y vi películas todo el día.
—¡Qué envidia! Necesito otro fin de semana para descansar.
translation:
—Good morning, Paola. How was your weekend?
—Very good, Andrés. On Saturday I had lunch with my parents, and in the evening I went out dancing with some friends. And yours?
—Good, but I didn't get any rest. My wife and I painted the whole apartment. We finished on Sunday at ten at night.
—Wow, how hard-working! I, on the other hand, didn't do anything useful: on Sunday I slept until eleven and watched movies all day.
—I'm so jealous! I need another weekend to rest.

questions.q: What are Paola and Andrés talking about?
options: What they did over the weekend
A new colleague at the office
questions.explain: Andrés asks '¿Cómo te fue el fin de semana?', and both talk about their Saturday and Sunday.

questions.q: Who did Andrés paint the apartment with?
questions.explain: Andrés says 'Mi esposa y yo pintamos todo el apartamento'.

questions.q: Paola says '¡Uy, qué juicioso!' What does she mean?
questions.explain: She says it after Andrés tells her about all his work, and then adds 'Yo, en cambio, no hice nada útil'.

topic: a power outage at home
title: Se fue la luz
text:
El jueves por la noche, la familia Rojas estaba en la casa. A las ocho, mientras comían, se fue la luz. ¡Todo el barrio quedó a oscuras!

La mamá buscó unas velas y el papá las prendió. No había televisión ni internet, y los celulares tenían poca batería. Entonces, el papá sacó unas cartas y todos jugaron en la mesa del comedor. Se rieron mucho.

A las diez, volvió la luz. Pero los niños no quisieron prender el televisor. “¡Uno más, por favor!”, dijeron.
translation:
On Thursday evening, the Rojas family was at home. At eight, while they were eating, the power went out. The whole neighborhood was left in the dark!

Mom looked for some candles and Dad lit them. There was no TV or internet, and the cell phones had little battery left. So Dad took out some cards and everyone played at the dining table. They laughed a lot.

At ten, the power came back. But the children didn't want to turn on the TV. “One more, please!” they said.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A family dinner at a restaurant
A birthday party for the kids
A broken TV in the living room
questions.explain: At eight 'se fue la luz', and at ten 'volvió la luz'.

questions.q: What did the mom look for?
questions.explain: The text says 'La mamá buscó unas velas'.

questions.q: Why didn't the children want to turn on the TV?
questions.explain: Everyone played cards and laughed a lot, and now the children say '¡Uno más, por favor!'

topic: restaurant booking for Mother's Day
title: Reserva para el Día de la Madre
text:
Asunto: Reserva para el Día de la Madre

Buenos días:
Me llamo Felipe Ortiz. Quiero hacer una reserva para el almuerzo del Día de la Madre, el domingo 9 de mayo, a la una de la tarde. Somos nueve personas: siete adultos y dos niños. Mi mamá usa silla de ruedas, por eso necesitamos una mesa en el primer piso.

Tengo dos preguntas: ¿tienen menú para niños? ¿Hay parqueadero?
Muchas gracias. Quedo atento a su respuesta.
Felipe Ortiz
Celular: 315 555 0823
translation:
Subject: Reservation for Mother's Day

Good morning,
My name is Felipe Ortiz. I would like to make a reservation for lunch on Mother's Day, Sunday, May 9, at one in the afternoon. There are nine of us: seven adults and two children. My mom uses a wheelchair, so we need a table on the first floor.

I have two questions: do you have a children's menu? Is there a parking lot?
Thank you very much. I look forward to your reply.
Felipe Ortiz
Cell phone: 315 555 0823

questions.q: Why does Felipe write this email?
options: To change the day of a booking
To cancel a table for Sunday
To book a table for a family lunch
To ask for the restaurant's prices
questions.explain: Felipe writes 'Quiero hacer una reserva para el almuerzo del Día de la Madre'.

questions.q: Why does the family need a table on the first floor?
options: The second floor is too noisy
His father has a broken leg
questions.explain: Felipe writes 'Mi mamá usa silla de ruedas, por eso necesitamos una mesa en el primer piso'.

questions.q: Felipe writes 'Quedo atento a su respuesta.' What does he mean?
questions.explain: 'Respuesta' means reply, and 'quedo atento' means I stay attentive: he is waiting for the restaurant to answer.

topic: exchanging a shirt at a store
title: Un cambio en la tienda
text:
—Buenas tardes. ¿En qué le puedo colaborar?
—Buenas tardes. El sábado compré esta camisa para mi esposo, pero le quedó pequeña. ¿La puedo cambiar?
—Claro. ¿Tiene la factura?
—Sí, aquí está.
—¿Qué talla necesita?
—Esta es talla M. Necesito una L, en el mismo color.
—Qué pena con usted, pero en azul ya no hay L. Hay en gris o en negro.
—Mmm… A él no le gusta el negro. Entonces, la gris.
—Perfecto. ¿Se la empaco para regalo?
—No, gracias. Así está bien.
translation:
—Good afternoon. How can I help you?
—Good afternoon. On Saturday I bought this shirt for my husband, but it was too small for him. Can I exchange it?
—Of course. Do you have the receipt?
—Yes, here it is.
—What size do you need?
—This one is a size M. I need an L, in the same color.
—I'm so sorry, but we don't have any more L's in blue. We have it in gray or in black.
—Hmm… He doesn't like black. The gray one, then.
—Perfect. Shall I gift-wrap it for you?
—No, thanks. It's fine like this.

questions.q: What does the customer want to do?
options: Get her money back for a shirt
Find a shirt in her own size
Buy a second shirt in blue
questions.explain: She says 'compré esta camisa para mi esposo' and asks '¿La puedo cambiar?'

questions.q: What is the problem with the shirt?
options: It's too small for her husband
It's too big for her husband
It has a small hole in the back
questions.explain: The customer says 'le quedó pequeña'.

questions.q: Which shirt does the customer take in the end?
questions.explain: She needs an L, there is no L 'en azul', her husband doesn't like black, and she says 'Entonces, la gris'.

topic: a couple moving to a new apartment
title: El trasteo
text:
El sábado, Camilo y Daniela hicieron su trasteo. Dejaron su apartamento pequeño en Chapinero y se fueron a uno más grande en Teusaquillo.

Tres amigos los ayudaron con las cajas. Pero hubo un problema: el edificio nuevo no tiene ascensor y el apartamento queda en el cuarto piso. Subir la nevera y el sofá por las escaleras fue muy difícil.

Por la noche, todos estaban cansados. Comieron pizza en el piso de la sala, entre cajas. ¡Su primera cena en la casa nueva!
translation:
On Saturday, Camilo and Daniela moved. They left their small apartment in Chapinero and went to a bigger one in Teusaquillo.

Three friends helped them with the boxes. But there was a problem: the new building has no elevator, and the apartment is on the fourth floor. Carrying the fridge and the sofa up the stairs was very hard.

In the evening, everyone was tired. They ate pizza on the living room floor, among the boxes. Their first dinner in their new home!

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A party in a new apartment
A couple looking for an apartment
A couple moving to a new home
questions.explain: Camilo and Daniela left Chapinero and 'se fueron a uno más grande en Teusaquillo'.

questions.q: Who helped Camilo and Daniela?
questions.explain: The text says 'Tres amigos los ayudaron con las cajas'.

questions.q: 'El apartamento queda en el cuarto piso.' What does 'queda' mean here?
questions.explain: 'Queda en el cuarto piso' says where the apartment is, so 'queda' means 'is located'.

topic: office collection for a retiring colleague
title: Un regalo para don Jorge
text:
Natalia: ¡Hola, equipo! El viernes es el último día de don Jorge en la oficina. ¡Se va a pensionar después de veinte años!
Natalia: Vamos a hacer una vaca para comprarle un regalo. Cada uno pone veinte mil pesos. ¿Qué les parece?
Julián: ¡De una! Mañana te doy mi parte.
Carolina: Listo. ¿Y qué le compramos?
Natalia: A él le encanta el café. Pensé en una cafetera y una libra de café del Huila.
Carolina: ¡Perfecto! Yo compro una tarjeta y todos la firmamos.
translation:
Natalia: Hi, team! Friday is don Jorge's last day at the office. He's retiring after twenty years!
Natalia: We're going to pool our money to buy him a present. Everyone puts in twenty thousand pesos. What do you think?
Julián: Count me in! I'll give you my share tomorrow.
Carolina: OK. And what are we getting him?
Natalia: He loves coffee. I was thinking of a coffee maker and a pound of coffee from Huila.
Carolina: Perfect! I'll buy a card and we'll all sign it.

questions.q: What is the chat mainly about?
options: Plans to say goodbye to a colleague
Plans for a colleague's birthday party
A problem with the office computers
Plans to welcome a new colleague
questions.explain: Natalia writes that Friday is 'el último día de don Jorge en la oficina'.

questions.q: What does don Jorge love?
questions.explain: Natalia writes 'A él le encanta el café'.

questions.q: Natalia writes 'Vamos a hacer una vaca'. What does she want to do?
options: Visit a farm outside the city
Make a list of gift ideas
questions.explain: Right after it she writes 'Cada uno pone veinte mil pesos', so everyone puts money together for the present.

topic: recipe for fried green plantains
title: Cómo hacer patacones
text:
PATACONES

Ingredientes: dos plátanos verdes, aceite y sal.

1. Pela los plátanos y córtalos en pedazos de tres centímetros.
2. Calienta aceite en una sartén y fríe los pedazos cinco minutos.
3. Sácalos y aplástalos con una pataconera o con el fondo de un plato. Deben quedar redondos y planos.
4. Fríelos otra vez dos o tres minutos, hasta dorarlos.
5. Ponlos en papel absorbente y échales sal.
Sírvelos calientes con hogao o queso. En la costa, los comen con pescado frito.
translation:
PATACONES

Ingredients: two green plantains, oil and salt.

1. Peel the plantains and cut them into three-centimeter pieces.
2. Heat oil in a frying pan and fry the pieces for five minutes.
3. Take them out and flatten them with a pataconera or with the bottom of a plate. They should be round and flat.
4. Fry them again for two or three minutes, until they are golden.
5. Put them on paper towels and sprinkle them with salt.
Serve them hot with hogao or cheese. On the coast, people eat them with fried fish.

questions.q: What does this text explain?
options: How to make a tomato sauce
How to make a plantain dish
questions.explain: It lists 'dos plátanos verdes, aceite y sal' and gives the steps to make patacones.

questions.q: How long do you fry the pieces the first time?
questions.explain: Step 2 says 'fríe los pedazos cinco minutos'.

questions.q: What is a 'pataconera'?
options: A tool to flatten the pieces
A pan to fry the pieces in
A plate to serve the food on
A knife to cut the pieces
questions.explain: You 'aplástalos con una pataconera o con el fondo de un plato' until they are 'planos', so it is a tool for flattening them.

topic: driving restriction day in Bogotá
title: Un miércoles sin carro
text:
Álvaro trabaja en el centro de Bogotá y siempre va en carro. El miércoles salió de la casa a las siete. Pero cuando abrió el garaje, su hija Valentina le gritó desde la ventana: “¡Papá, hoy tienes pico y placa!”.

Álvaro miró la placa: su hija tenía razón. Entonces caminó hasta la estación y tomó un bus. El bus iba lleno, pero allí encontró a un viejo amigo del colegio. Hablaron todo el camino y el tiempo pasó muy rápido.
translation:
Álvaro works in downtown Bogotá and always goes by car. On Wednesday he left the house at seven. But when he opened the garage, his daughter Valentina shouted from the window: “Dad, today you have pico y placa!”

Álvaro looked at the license plate: his daughter was right. So he walked to the station and took a bus. The bus was full, but there he ran into an old friend from school. They talked the whole way, and the time went by very fast.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A day off with his daughter
A visit to Álvaro's old school
questions.explain: Álvaro 'siempre va en carro', but this Wednesday he 'tomó un bus'.

questions.q: Who did Álvaro meet on the way?
questions.explain: The text says 'allí encontró a un viejo amigo del colegio'.

questions.q: What is 'pico y placa'?
options: A problem with the car's engine
A big traffic jam in the city
A rule about when you can drive
A day without buses in Bogotá
questions.explain: When Valentina says it, Álvaro checks the car's 'placa' (license plate) and leaves the car at home: it is a rule that keeps some cars off the road on some days.

topic: taxi ride to the airport
title: Un taxi al aeropuerto
text:
—Buenas tardes. ¿Me lleva al aeropuerto, por favor?
—Claro. ¿A qué hora es su vuelo?
—A las seis y media. ¿Llegamos a tiempo?
—A esta hora siempre hay trancón en la calle 26, y hoy es viernes. Vamos a tardar una hora.
—¡Una hora! El domingo hice el mismo viaje en veinte minutos.
—Sí, pero los domingos no hay tantos carros. Tranquila, conozco otro camino.
(…)
—Listo, señora. Llegamos. Son las cinco y cuarto.
—¡Qué bien! Gracias. ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta?
—Claro que sí.
translation:
—Good afternoon. Can you take me to the airport, please?
—Sure. What time is your flight?
—At six thirty. Will we get there on time?
—At this time of day there's always a traffic jam on Calle 26, and today is Friday. It's going to take us an hour.
—An hour! On Sunday I made the same trip in twenty minutes.
—Yes, but on Sundays there aren't so many cars. Don't worry, I know another way.
(…)
—Here we are, ma'am. It's a quarter past five.
—Great! Thank you. Can I pay by card?
—Of course.

questions.q: Why is the passenger worried?
options: She may be late for her flight
She doesn't have cash to pay
The driver doesn't know the way
She left her passport at home
questions.explain: She asks '¿Llegamos a tiempo?', and the driver says 'Vamos a tardar una hora'.

questions.q: What time is her flight?
questions.explain: She says 'A las seis y media'.

questions.q: What is a 'trancón'?
questions.explain: The driver says there is always 'trancón' at this hour, but 'los domingos no hay tantos carros': it is a traffic jam.

topic: complaint about a damaged online order
title: Una licuadora rota
text:
Asunto: Licuadora rota (pedido 4582)

Buenas tardes:
El lunes compré una licuadora en su página web. El pedido llegó ayer, pero cuando abrí la caja, vi que el vaso estaba roto. Además, faltaba la tapa: en la caja solo venían el vaso y la base. Les envío dos fotos.

Necesito la licuadora todos los días para los jugos de mis hijos. Por eso, quiero recibir una nueva esta semana. Si no es posible, por favor devuélvanme el dinero.
Gracias,
Martha Pérez
translation:
Subject: Broken blender (order 4582)

Good afternoon,
On Monday I bought a blender on your website. The order arrived yesterday, but when I opened the box, I saw that the jar was broken. Also, the lid was missing: only the jar and the base came in the box. I'm sending you two photos.

I need the blender every day for my children's juice. So I want to receive a new one this week. If that isn't possible, please give me my money back.
Thank you,
Martha Pérez

questions.q: Why does Martha write to the store?
options: She paid twice for her order
questions.explain: She writes that when she opened the box, 'el vaso estaba roto'.

questions.q: What does Martha want first?
options: A discount on her next order
questions.explain: She writes 'quiero recibir una nueva esta semana'; she wants her money back only if that is not possible.

questions.q: Martha writes 'Además, faltaba la tapa'. What does this mean?
options: The lid was not in the box
The lid was the wrong color
questions.explain: She adds 'en la caja solo venían el vaso y la base', so the lid was missing.

topic: a job interview by video call
title: La entrevista
text:
El martes, Sara tuvo una entrevista de trabajo por videollamada. Se puso una blusa elegante, preparó un tinto y se sentó frente al computador.

Todo iba muy bien. La jefa de recursos humanos le hacía preguntas y Sara respondía con calma. Pero de repente, alguien tocó el timbre y su perro Rocky empezó a ladrar muy fuerte. Sara se puso roja.

La jefa se rio y le dijo: “Tranquila, yo tengo dos gatos”. Dos días después, Sara recibió un correo: ¡consiguió el trabajo!
translation:
On Tuesday, Sara had a job interview by video call. She put on an elegant blouse, made herself a black coffee and sat down in front of the computer.

Everything was going very well. The head of human resources was asking her questions, and Sara was answering calmly. But suddenly, someone rang the doorbell and her dog Rocky started barking very loudly. Sara turned red.

The manager laughed and said: “Don't worry, I have two cats.” Two days later, Sara got an email: she got the job!

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: Sara's first day working from home
A job interview by video call
A video call with Sara's family
A problem with Sara's new computer
questions.explain: Sara 'tuvo una entrevista de trabajo por videollamada'.

questions.q: Why did Rocky start barking?
options: He saw a cat on the screen
questions.explain: The text says 'alguien tocó el timbre y su perro Rocky empezó a ladrar'.

questions.q: Why did the woman on the call say 'Tranquila, yo tengo dos gatos'?
options: To show she was not annoyed
To ask Sara to look after her cats
To explain that she doesn't like dogs
questions.explain: She laughs and says 'Tranquila' (relax): she has pets too, so the barking is not a problem for her.

topic: recycling rules in an apartment complex
title: Aviso: separación de basuras
text:
CONJUNTO RESIDENCIAL LOS PINOS
AVISO PARA TODOS LOS RESIDENTES

A partir del próximo lunes, vamos a separar la basura en dos bolsas:
Bolsa blanca: plástico, vidrio, papel, cartón y latas. Todo debe estar limpio y seco.
Bolsa negra: restos de comida, papel higiénico, servilletas sucias y otros residuos.

El camión de reciclaje pasa los martes y los viernes por la mañana. Por favor, saquen las bolsas al cuarto de basuras la noche anterior, nunca al pasillo.
¡Gracias por cuidar el planeta!
La Administración
translation:
LOS PINOS RESIDENTIAL COMPLEX
NOTICE TO ALL RESIDENTS

Starting next Monday, we are going to separate our trash into two bags:
White bag: plastic, glass, paper, cardboard and cans. Everything must be clean and dry.
Black bag: food scraps, toilet paper, dirty napkins and other waste.

The recycling truck comes on Tuesday and Friday mornings. Please take the bags to the trash room the night before, never to the hallway.
Thank you for taking care of the planet!
The Management

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To explain a new way to sort trash
To ask residents to buy special bags
To say the trash room is closing
To ask residents to clean the hallways
questions.explain: The notice says 'vamos a separar la basura en dos bolsas'.

questions.q: What goes in the black bag?
questions.explain: The notice says 'Bolsa negra: restos de comida, papel higiénico, servilletas sucias…'.

questions.q: It is Monday night. What should you do with your white bag?
options: Keep it at home until Friday
Take it to the trash room
Put it out on the street
questions.explain: The recycling truck comes on Tuesday morning, and the bags go 'al cuarto de basuras la noche anterior'.

topic: a first salsa dance class
title: Mi primera clase de salsa
text:
Querido diario:
Hoy fui a mi primera clase de salsa. Hace años que quiero aprender, porque en las fiestas todos bailan y yo siempre me quedo sentada.

El profesor, Wilson, es de Cali, la ciudad de la salsa. Al principio estaba nerviosa y le pisé los pies a mi pareja tres veces. ¡Qué vergüenza! Pero Wilson fue muy paciente y al final ya podía hacer los pasos básicos.

El jueves vuelvo. ¡En diciembre quiero bailar en la fiesta de la oficina!
translation:
Dear diary,
Today I went to my first salsa class. I've wanted to learn for years, because at parties everyone dances and I always stay in my seat.

The teacher, Wilson, is from Cali, the city of salsa. At first I was nervous, and I stepped on my partner's feet three times. How embarrassing! But Wilson was very patient, and by the end I could already do the basic steps.

I'm going back on Thursday. In December I want to dance at the office party!

questions.q: Why did the writer start taking salsa classes?
options: Her doctor told her to exercise
Her boyfriend is a salsa teacher
She wants to dance at parties
She wants to meet new people
questions.explain: She writes 'en las fiestas todos bailan y yo siempre me quedo sentada'.

questions.q: Where is the teacher from?
questions.explain: She writes 'El profesor, Wilson, es de Cali'.

questions.q: She writes '¡Qué vergüenza!' How did she feel?
questions.explain: She says it right after 'le pisé los pies a mi pareja tres veces'.

topic: planning a family riverside cookout
title: Plan para el puente
text:
Tía Rosa: ¡Hola, familia! Para el puente vamos a hacer un paseo de olla al río. ¿Quiénes se animan?
Andrés: ¡Nosotros vamos! ¿Qué llevamos?
Tía Rosa: Yo llevo la olla grande, el pollo y la leña. Ustedes traen las papas, la yuca y el plátano para el sancocho.
Laura: Nosotros llevamos las gaseosas, el hielo y la música.
Andrés: ¿A qué hora salimos?
Tía Rosa: A las seis de la mañana, para conseguir un buen puesto al lado del río. ¡Y lleven bloqueador!
translation:
Aunt Rosa: Hi, family! For the long weekend we're going to have a paseo de olla by the river. Who wants to come?
Andrés: We're going! What should we bring?
Aunt Rosa: I'll bring the big pot, the chicken and the firewood. You bring the potatoes, the yuca and the plantain for the sancocho.
Laura: We'll bring the sodas, the ice and the music.
Andrés: What time are we leaving?
Aunt Rosa: At six in the morning, to get a good spot next to the river. And bring sunscreen!

questions.q: What is the chat mainly about?
options: Plans for a trip with friends
questions.explain: Aunt Rosa writes '¡Hola, familia!' and asks '¿Quiénes se animan?'

questions.q: What does Laura offer to bring?
options: Chairs, a tent and a ball
questions.explain: Laura writes 'Nosotros llevamos las gaseosas, el hielo y la música'.

questions.q: What is a 'paseo de olla'?
options: A trip where people cook outdoors
A trip to a restaurant by a river
A boat trip on the river
A trip to buy pots and pans
questions.explain: They take 'la olla grande', 'la leña' and the vegetables 'para el sancocho' to the river, so they cook there.

topic: doctor's visit for a twisted ankle
title: En el consultorio
text:
—Buenos días. Siga y siéntese. ¿Qué le pasó?
—Ayer estaba jugando fútbol y me caí. Me torcí el tobillo derecho.
—¿Le duele mucho?
—Sí, sobre todo cuando camino. Anoche no pude dormir.
—A ver… Mueva el pie. Bueno, no está roto. Tiene que descansar una semana y ponerse hielo tres veces al día.
—¿Una semana? ¡Pero yo soy mesero y trabajo todo el día de pie!
—Tranquilo. Le voy a dar una incapacidad de cinco días. Así no tiene que ir al restaurante.
translation:
—Good morning. Come in and sit down. What happened to you?
—Yesterday I was playing soccer and I fell. I twisted my right ankle.
—Does it hurt a lot?
—Yes, especially when I walk. Last night I couldn't sleep.
—Let's see… Move your foot. Well, it isn't broken. You have to rest for a week and put ice on it three times a day.
—A week? But I'm a waiter, and I'm on my feet all day!
—Don't worry. I'm going to give you a sick note for five days. That way you don't have to go to the restaurant.

questions.q: Why did the man go to the doctor?
options: He broke his leg playing soccer
He hurt his back at work
He hurt his ankle playing soccer
He fell down the stairs at home
questions.explain: He says 'estaba jugando fútbol y me caí. Me torcí el tobillo derecho'.

questions.q: What does the doctor tell him to do?
options: Take some pills and keep on working
Walk a lot to make it stronger
Come back tomorrow for an X-ray
Rest and use ice three times a day
questions.explain: The doctor says 'Tiene que descansar una semana y ponerse hielo tres veces al día'.

questions.q: The doctor gives him 'una incapacidad'. What is it?
options: A medicine to take for the pain
A paper that lets him miss work
A bill to pay for the visit
questions.explain: He is a waiter, and with the 'incapacidad de cinco días' he 'no tiene que ir al restaurante': it is a sick note.

topic: a neighbor's noisy party
title: La fiesta de arriba
text:
Era medianoche y Lorena todavía no podía dormir. En el apartamento de arriba había una fiesta y la música sonaba cada vez más fuerte.

A la una, cansada y de mal genio, subió a quejarse. Le abrió la puerta un señor mayor que sonreía.
—Perdone el ruido, vecina. Es que mi nieta se graduó hoy de médica. ¡Siga y cómase un pedacito de torta!

Lorena iba a decir que no, pero no pudo. Al final, bailó con el abuelo hasta las tres.
translation:
It was midnight, and Lorena still couldn't sleep. There was a party in the apartment upstairs, and the music was getting louder and louder.

At one o'clock, tired and in a bad mood, she went up to complain. A smiling older man opened the door.
—Sorry about the noise, neighbor. You see, my granddaughter graduated as a doctor today. Come in and have a little piece of cake!

Lorena was going to say no, but she couldn't. In the end, she danced with the grandfather until three.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A party Lorena gives for her family
A night out dancing with friends
A noisy night with a happy ending
A neighbor who complains about Lorena
questions.explain: Lorena 'no podía dormir' because of a party upstairs, but in the end she danced there until three.

questions.q: Why was there a party upstairs?
options: A big soccer win for Colombia
questions.explain: The man says 'Es que mi nieta se graduó hoy de médica'.

questions.q: Lorena went upstairs 'de mal genio'. What does this mean?
options: She was in a big hurry
She was in a bad mood
questions.explain: It was one in the morning, the music did not let her sleep, and she went up 'a quejarse' (to complain).

topic: school field trip email to parents
title: Salida pedagógica
text:
Asunto: Salida pedagógica al Jardín Botánico

Apreciados padres de familia:
El próximo viernes, los estudiantes de tercero van a hacer una salida pedagógica al Jardín Botánico. Allí van a conocer plantas de diferentes regiones de Colombia.

Salimos a las 8:00 a. m. y regresamos a la 1:00 p. m. Los niños deben ir con la sudadera del colegio y llevar gorra y un refrigerio: una fruta, un sándwich y agua. Por favor, envíen la autorización firmada antes del miércoles.
Cordialmente,
Profesora Marcela Díaz
translation:
Subject: School trip to the Botanical Garden

Dear parents,
Next Friday, the third-grade students are going on a school trip to the Botanical Garden. There they are going to see plants from different regions of Colombia.

We leave at 8:00 a.m. and come back at 1:00 p.m. The children must wear the school tracksuit and bring a cap and a snack: a piece of fruit, a sandwich and water. Please send the signed permission form before Wednesday.
Best regards,
Ms. Marcela Díaz

questions.q: Why does the teacher write to the parents?
options: To say that a class trip is canceled
To invite parents to a garden party
To ask parents to drive on a trip
To give details of a class trip
questions.explain: She writes that the students 'van a hacer una salida pedagógica al Jardín Botánico'.

questions.q: What time do the children come back?
questions.explain: The email says 'regresamos a la 1:00 p. m.'

questions.q: What is a 'refrigerio'?
questions.explain: The email explains it right after the colon: 'una fruta, un sándwich y agua'.

topic: a family's New Year's Eve traditions
title: Doce uvas y una maleta
text:
El 31 de diciembre, Luis y su familia recibieron el año nuevo donde los abuelos.

A las doce, cada uno se comió doce uvas y pidió un deseo con cada una. Después, el tío Hernán salió corriendo con una maleta vacía y le dio la vuelta a la cuadra, porque quiere viajar mucho. La abuela les dio unas lentejas para el bolsillo: según ella, así nunca les va a faltar la plata.

Luis no sabe si estas tradiciones funcionan, pero le encantan.
translation:
On December 31, Luis and his family welcomed the new year at his grandparents' house.

At twelve o'clock, each of them ate twelve grapes and made a wish with each one. Then Uncle Hernán ran out with an empty suitcase and went around the block, because he wants to travel a lot. Grandma gave them some lentils for their pockets: according to her, that way they will never be short of money.

Luis doesn't know if these traditions work, but he loves them.

questions.q: What is the story mainly about?
options: A New Year's trip to the beach
A New Year's party with friends
The uncle's trip abroad in January
questions.explain: On 'el 31 de diciembre' the family does several things for the new year, and the text calls them 'estas tradiciones'.

questions.q: What did each person do with the twelve grapes?
options: Made a wish with each one
questions.explain: The text says 'cada uno se comió doce uvas y pidió un deseo con cada una'.

questions.q: Uncle Hernán 'le dio la vuelta a la cuadra'. What did he do?
options: He waited at the street corner
He went to visit a neighbor
He ran to the bus station
questions.explain: 'La cuadra' is the block, and 'le dio la vuelta' means he went all the way around it.
